name: Nepal

findings.summary: Huawei built state-owned Nepal Telecom's 3G and 4G radio infrastructure; the operator's 2G-4G networks run on Chinese radio and core equipment, and Huawei is to keep supporting existing services.
findings.analyst_inference: Date 2017 is the 4G launch in Kathmandu/Pokhara; Huawei's 3G build predates it. still_current true because December 2025 reporting says Huawei will continue supporting 2G-4G services. Not corroborated: all opened sources are S3, no S1/S2.

findings.summary: Nepal Telecom signed three contracts in February 2019 for a Rs19bn nationwide 4G expansion: ZTE supplied the core network and Hong Kong-based CCSI the radio access network with Huawei; service expanded to 20+ cities from October 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5 on reported nationwide launch in October 2019. ZTE's core quote was Rs1.56bn; total project Rs19bn (not converted). CCSI is a China Communications Services subsidiary, so the RAN side is also PRC-linked. still_current not confirmed in this pass for the ZTE core specifically. Not corroborated: no opened S1/S2 source.

findings.reversal_of: Nepal Telecom 5G trials on Huawei/ZTE equipment (trial permit November 2021)
findings.summary: Nepal Telecom's 5G trials with Huawei and ZTE equipment, held in Kathmandu, Pokhara and Birgunj, were called off after it could not obtain a permit to import Chinese equipment; US and Indian officials reportedly objected to non-competitive vendor selection.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded regulatory because the stated proximate cause is an unresolved import permit between operator and regulator; the geopolitical explanation (US/Indian embassy concerns) is reported as attributed or speculative. A reviewer may reclassify as geopolitical. Scale subnational because trials covered selected cities.

findings.summary: Nepal Telecom decided to launch 5G in standalone mode with a new cloud-native core and dedicated radio network bought through open competitive bidding, which would effectively end Huawei's role for 5G; no tender timeline was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no vendor selected. Not coded as a reversal because no Huawei 5G contract existed to cancel; it is a statement of procurement intent. Whether any 5G tender has since been issued or awarded was not established in this pass.

findings.reversal_of: Nepal Telecom convergent real-time billing and customer support system tender (Huawei expected shortlist)
findings.summary: Nepal Telecom's board cancelled a roughly Rs5.5bn tender for a new real-time billing and customer-support system in January 2026; only Huawei and Whale Cloud bid, Huawei was reportedly to be shortlisted, and the US Embassy reportedly objected.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 because the reversed item was a tender at technical evaluation with no award. reversal_reason geopolitical rests on Republica's unnamed sources and its report of US Embassy concerns; Kantipur and Nepali Times give no reason, and the minister cited controversy. The incumbent billing system is from Chinese firm AsiaInfo, so the stack stays PRC-supplied for now. Not corroborated: no opened S1/S2.

findings.summary: Nepal Telecom signed a letter of intent with Huawei to build a NPR 484m primary data centre in Kathmandu and a disaster-recovery site in Bhairahawa; specifications and final terms were undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic under the owner-operator rule (state-owned Nepal Telecom); Huawei is recorded as builder. If Huawei also supplies the IT equipment, a separate PRC equipment finding would apply. Value USD 3.5m as reported by DCD (converted by the source). Tier 1 (LOI only); whether a contract followed was not checked.

findings.controller: Yotta Data Services / BLC Holding joint venture
findings.summary: India's Yotta Data Services and Nepal's BLC Holding formed a joint venture to build K1, a Tier III data centre of up to 4MW near Kathmandu airport, pitched for cloud and AI workloads and targeted for completion within 24 months.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: ownership split and day-to-day operator of the JV are not stated, so control could be third (India) or domestic. Tier 2 (JV formed, no financing close or construction start confirmed). Investment described only as multi-million dollar. The 24-month target (about April 2026) has passed; completion not checked.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases surfaced in network, data-centre or AI-policy searches; no dedicated silicon search within budget

models.null_reason: National AI Policy 2025 approved by cabinet (August 2025) sets up a National AI Centre but names no model provider or national model; no government model partnership found

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power evidence surfaced; AI policy mentions cold-climate data-centre siting only
